verified_findings.claim: Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man publicly characterized the So Min-ho shooting case on May 10 as an individual criminal matter rather than a political case.
verified_findings.caution: This is the prosecution's contemporaneous characterization, not a neutral final judicial finding.

verified_findings.claim: The So Min-ho trip itself was connected to inspection of the newly held local-council elections and investigation of local grievances, creating a direct bridge between the 1952 local-election corpus and the constitutional-crisis actor graph.
National Archives confirms the July 4 constitutional vote at 166 present and 163 in favor, independently matching FRUS/UN-derived figures.

AKS identifies a more granular July 4 coercion layer: police and military surrounding the Assembly and Nam Song-hak plus younger Liberal-unification/Silla-hoe legislators controlling access during the standing vote.
verified_findings.caution: Named access-control roles require original Assembly/police records before being treated as complete operational command chain.

verified_findings.claim: UN Yearbook's summary of A/2187 attributes the May 25 emergency martial-law implementation to the State Council chaired by the President, while separately recording the Martial Law Commander's claim that he was responsible only to the President.
verified_findings.caution: Institutional responsibility does not itself identify each arrest order's author.

verified_findings.claim: FRUS d163 preserves Chang Taek-sang's contemporaneous account that most ministers resisted dissolution, Yi Pom-sok proposed putting all Assembly members in a stockade, and Rhee instructed Yi not to prevent demonstrators entering Busan.
verified_findings.caution: Still a US diplomatic report of Chang's account, pending Korean Cabinet minutes.

verified_findings.claim: FRUS d206 and National Archives agree on the 163-0-3 July 4 outcome; AKS adds Korean secondary institutional detail on physical access control. This forms a three-provenance bundle but does not by itself resolve legal validity or individual coercion attribution.

adversarial_checks: Han Kyok-man's statement that the So Min-ho case was nonpolitical is a prosecution position and cannot settle the later political use of the case.
The So Min-ho shooting predates martial-law re-arrest; do not retroactively treat the shooting itself as a martial-law event.
State Council responsibility for martial law does not prove unanimous Cabinet support for Assembly dissolution; FRUS d163 reports the opposite on June 3.
The Martial Law Commander's claimed responsibility to the President does not identify who authored each arrest order.
The 163-0-3 vote is independently corroborated, but numerical unanimity cannot be read as proof of uncoerced consent.
AKS's access-control attribution to Nam Song-hak and allied legislators is not yet an original police/Assembly command record.
Rhee's June popular-mandate assertions remain party statements until provincial/local resolutions are individually verified.
Chang Taek-sang's d163 account is contemporaneous but one provenance family; Korean Cabinet minutes remain necessary.
US contingency planning in June 1952 is not evidence that a removal/intervention plan was executed.
Assassination-case prosecution allegations and contemporary press descriptions must remain separate from final judicial findings.

history_debt_updates.update: UN A/2187/Yearbook adds institutional attribution for May 25 martial law to the State Council and a claimed President-only reporting line for the Martial Law Commander; individual arrest/order authorship remains unresolved.
